Level 1: HTML Basics

My First Webpage

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <title>My First Webpage</title>
    </head>
    <body>
        <h1>Hello World!</h1>
        <p>This is my first webpage.</p>
    </body>
</html>

Code copied!

This is a basic HTML example. It shows the structure of a webpage with a heading and a paragraph.

Level 2: CSS Styling

Styled Webpage

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <title>Styled Webpage</title>
        <style>
            body {
                background-color: #f0f0f0;
                color: #333;
            }
            h1 {
                color: blue;
            }
            p {
                font-size: 16px;
            }
        </style>
    </head>
    <body>
        <h1>Hello World!</h1>
        <p>This is my styled webpage.</p>
    </body>
</html>

Code copied!

This example demonstrates how to add CSS styles to your HTML to control the appearance of your webpage.

Level 3: JavaScript Basics

Interactive Webpage

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <title>Interactive Webpage</title>
    </head>
    <body>
        <h1>Hello World!</h1>
        <button onclick="myFunction()">Click Me</button>
        <script>
            function myFunction() {
                alert("Hello from JavaScript!");
            }
        </script>
    </body>
</html>

Code copied!

This example introduces JavaScript to make your webpage interactive. Clicking the button will trigger a JavaScript function.

Level 4: Advanced HTML

HTML with Forms and Tables

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <title>HTML Forms and Tables</title>
    </head>
    <body>
        <h2>HTML Forms</h2>
        <form action="/action_page.php">
            <label for="fname">First name:</label><br>
            <input type="text" id="fname" name="fname"<br><br>
            <label for="lname">Last name:</label><br>
            <input type="text" id="lname" name="lname"<br><br>
            <input type="submit" value="Submit">
        </form>
        <h2>HTML Table</h2>
        <table border="1">
            <tr>
                <th>Month</th>
                <th>Savings</th>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td>January</td>
                <td>$100</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td>February</td>
                <td>$50</td>
            </tr>
        </table>
    </body>
</html>

Code copied!

This example demonstrates more advanced HTML, including forms for user input and tables for displaying data in a structured format.

Level 5: Advanced CSS

Styled Navigation Menu

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Styled Navigation Menu</title>
    <style>
        ul {
            list-style-type: none;
            margin: 0;
            padding: 0;
            overflow: hidden;
            background-color: #333;
        }
        li {
            float: left;
        }
        li a {
            display: block;
            color: white;
            text-align: center;
            padding: 14px 16px;
            text-decoration: none;
        }
        li a:hover {
            background-color: #111;
        }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
<ul>
    <li><a href="#home">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="#news">News</a></li>
    <li><a href="#contact">Contact</a></li>
    <li><a href="#about">About</a></li>
</ul>
<h1>Welcome</h1>
<p>This is a styled navigation menu.</p>
</body>
</html>

Code copied!

This example demonstrates how to style a navigation menu using CSS, including creating a horizontal menu and styling the links.

Level 6: Advanced JavaScript

Dynamic List with JavaScript

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Dynamic List</title>
</head>
<body>
<ul id="myList"></ul>
<script>
    const listItems = ["Item 1", "Item 2", "Item 3"];
    const list = document.getElementById("myList");
    for (let i = 0; i < listItems.length; i++) {
        let listItem = document.createElement("li");
        listItem.textContent = listItems[i];        list.appendChild(listItem);
    }
</script>
</body>
</html>

Code copied!

This example demonstrates how to use JavaScript to dynamically create and populate a list in HTML. This is a fundamental concept in creating dynamic web pages.
